# Introduction

The **WolfPackR** package provides a comprehensive toolkit for analyzing the genetic and spatial structures of wolf packs. This vignette demonstrates how to use **WolfPackR** to analyze wolf pack territories, from genetic relatedness to spatial pack visualization, using both simulated and real-world datasets.

---

# Data Preparation

First, we load the necessary libraries and datasets provided with the package.

```{r load-libraries}
library(WolfPackR)
```

---

# Analysis Workflow

## 1. Simulated Dataset

### Genetic Groups

We start by identifying genetic groups using the `genetic_groups()` function. This function clusters individuals based on genetic relatedness.

```{r genetic-groups}
data("relate")
data("samples")

gengroups <- genetic_groups(relate, threshold = 0.4, estimator = "wang")
obs <- merge(samples, gengroups, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs, group)
```

### Ugly Ducklings

Next, we identify "ugly ducklings"—individuals that do not fit well into their assigned genetic groups—using the `ugly_ducklings()` function.

```{r ugly-ducklings}
ud_df <- ugly_ducklings(obs, group = group, min_overlap = 0.7, buffer = 0, mcp.percent = 100)
obs2 <- merge(samples, ud_df, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs2, new_group)
```

### Spatial Groups

Finally, we refine the spatial grouping of individuals using the `spatial_groups()` function, which clusters individuals based on spatial proximity.

```{r spatial-groups}
spatgroups <- spatial_groups(obs2, group = "new_group", percentile = 100,
                             buffer_radius = 0.0000001, max_iterations = 20, min_mcp_overlap = 0.6)
obs3 <- merge(samples, spatgroups, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs3, Subgroup)
```

---

## 2. Real-Life Dataset: Carpathian Wolves

### Genetic Groups

We apply the same workflow to a real-life dataset: 263 non-invasive genetic samples of 47 wolves (one of them a wolf x dog hybrid) collected in the Romanian Carpathians from 2017 to 2020 (Foundation Conservation Carpathia, 2024; Iosif et al., 2025).

Pairwise relatedness is first computed from the microsatellite genotypes with `relatedness()`. The wolf x dog hybrid EF.15J8 is left out of the allele frequencies. We use the Queller & Goodnight estimator with a threshold of 0.25, the value expected for second-degree relatives (first-degree relatives are expected at 0.5), so pairs above it are likely close kin. Because a few spurious links are unavoidable at such a threshold, groups are built by community detection (Leiden) rather than connected components, which would chain families together through single links.

```{r genetic-groups-carpat}
data("genotypes_Carpathians")
data("samples_Carpathians")

rel_carpat <- relatedness(genotypes_Carpathians,
                          freq_ids = setdiff(genotypes_Carpathians$Individual, "EF.15J8"))
gengroups_carpat <- genetic_groups(rel_carpat, estimator = "QG", threshold = 0.25, method = "leiden")
obs_carpat <- merge(samples_Carpathians, gengroups_carpat, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs_carpat, group)
```

### Ugly Ducklings

We identify "ugly ducklings" in the Carpathian dataset.

```{r ugly-ducklings-carpat}
ud_df_carpat <- ugly_ducklings(obs_carpat, group = group, min_overlap = 0.5, buffer = 0, mcp.percent = 100)
obs2_carpat <- merge(samples_Carpathians, ud_df_carpat, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs2_carpat, new_group)
```

### Spatial Groups

We refine the spatial grouping for the Carpathian dataset.

```{r spatial-groups-carpat}
spatgroups_carpat <- spatial_groups(obs2_carpat, group = "new_group", percentile = 100,
                             buffer_radius = 0.0000001, max_iterations = 20, min_mcp_overlap = 0.5)
obs3_carpat <- merge(samples_Carpathians, spatgroups_carpat, by = "Individual")
plot_packs(obs3_carpat, Subgroup)
```

---

# Conclusion

This vignette demonstrates the core functionality of **WolfPackR** for analyzing wolf pack territories using both simulated and real-world datasets. The package provides a robust framework for genetic and spatial analysis, enabling researchers to gain insights into wolf pack dynamics.

For more details, refer to the [WolfPackR GitHub repository](https://github.com/eboncourt/WolfPackR).
